key_decisions.rationale: Keeps congenital condition without defining the man by it, being carried, daily placement, gate name, and request.
key_decisions.before: A man who had been unable to walk from birth was being carried in. Every day people placed him at the temple gate called Beautiful so he could ask for alms from those entering the temple.
key_decisions.after: A man who had been unable to walk from his mother’s womb was being carried there. Every day people placed him at the temple gate called Beautiful so he could ask those entering for alms.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And a certain man, lame from his mother’s womb, was being carried, whom they were placing daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms from those entering into the temple.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves touch, body side, raising, immediacy, and body parts.
key_decisions.before: Taking him by the right hand, Peter raised him up. Immediately his feet and ankles became strong.
key_decisions.after: Taking him by the right hand, Peter raised him up. Immediately the man’s feet and ankles became strong.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And taking him by the right hand, he raised him up; and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves ancestral names, servant ambiguity, glory, handover, denial, Pilate, and release decision.
key_decisions.before: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our ancestors, glorified his servant Jesus. You handed him over and denied him before Pilate even though Pilate had decided to release him.
key_decisions.after: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the God of our ancestors—has glorified his servant Jesus. You handed him over and denied him before Pilate, even though Pilate had decided to release him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had decided to release him.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps titles, denial, request, murderer, and release.

key_decisions.after: You denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be released to you.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves sharp paradox, divine resurrection, and apostolic witness.

key_decisions.after: You killed the Author of life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps name, faith’s debated relation, public knowledge, strengthening, completeness, and witnesses.
key_decisions.before: Through trust in his name, his name has made this man strong—the man you see and know. The trust that comes through Jesus has given him this complete healing in front of you all.
key_decisions.after: By faith in Jesus’ name, his name has strengthened this man whom you see and know. The faith that comes through Jesus has given him this complete healing in front of all of you.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And by faith in his name, this one whom you see and know, his name has made strong; and the faith that is through him has given him this complete health in the presence of you all.
